## Introduction

The goal of today's workshop is to understand basic bash and git commands. Practice making a git directory. 

## Basics

- Change some files
- See what you changed  
  -- `git status`  
  -- `git diff`  
  -- `git log`  
- Decide what changes you want to save  
  -- `git add`  
- Commit those changes  
  -- `git commit`  
- Push changes to GitHub    
  -- `git push`  

## Basics

- Pull changes from collaborators  
  -- `git pull`  
  -- `git fetch`  
  -- `git merge`  


## Command line refresh

- Directory structure   
   -- Absolute    
    ~/Documents/Data422/Project/Rawdata/  
   -- Relative paths  
   ../Rawdata/  
- Creating, removing, changing directories  
  -- `mkdir`  
  -- `rmdir`  
  -- `cd`  
  -- `cd -`  
- Moving, copying, removing files  
  -- `mv`  
  -- `cp`  
  -- `rm -i`  
    
## Make a directory

```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
cd Documents/classes/reproducible_viz

mkdir workshop

cd workshop

cd ~

```

## Starting a new project
Create a local repository  

```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
pwd 
cd Documents/classes/reproducible_viz/workshop

touch workshopnotes.txt

git init

```


## What's inside?

Where does Git store information?
```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
ls
ls -a
```

`.git` extension:  
Git uses this special sub-directory to store all the information about the project, including all files and sub-directories located within the project’s directory.  

If we ever delete the `.git` sub-directory, we will lose the project’s history.

## Did it work?

```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
git status

```

## What's first?

```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
pwd 

cd ../Lecture

nano README.txt

touch dataprocessing.R 
```

A README file should describe the project and contents of the repository.  

`dataprocessing.R` will be an empty file but is an example of a code file.

## Stage Changes
```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}

git add README.txt

git add .
```
Tells git to start keeping track of this file  

Can add one file at a time or multiple

## Stage Changes
```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
git status

git add .

```

Can add one file at a time or multiple

## Incorporate changes into repository
```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
git commit

```

- Add file to the repository  
- The `-m` arguments allows you to add a message  
- Without the argument will open a text editor   
- Message can be multiple lines but first should be an overview  

## Checks
```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
git status

git log

```

## When to commit?
- Use frequent small commits  
- Commit sources not derived files  
- Use a `.gitignore` to indicate which files not to commit  


## What makes a good commit?
Why do you want to make small commits?

What makes a good commit message?

## Removing and moving files tracked by git
Use with caution!

```{bash, eval = FALSE, echo =TRUE}
git rm myfile

git mv myfile directory/newname

git commit

```
